summary: Retested secure AI ingestion, seeded-role authentication, viewer camera RBAC, and all nine admin navigation pages. Backend checks passed; UI routes rendered, but browser console warnings/errors remain for telemetry WebSocket setup and chart/markup rendering.

ui_bugs.issue: Browser console reports Recharts ResponsiveContainer width(-1)/height(-1) during page rendering; charts should avoid rendering until the container has measurable dimensions.
Browser console reports invalid HTML nesting: span cannot be a child of option, indicating a markup warning in a rendered control.

integration_issues.issue: Console reports wss WebSocket closed before connection establishment and WS error while navigating authenticated pages; live telemetry connection was not established in the public UI run.

action_items: Investigate public ingress/proxy support for wss /api/ws/telemetry and ensure the frontend reconnects without repeated console errors.
Fix invalid span-inside-option markup in the relevant select control.
Guard or resize Recharts ResponsiveContainer instances so initial layout does not produce zero/negative dimension warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py remains a very large monolithic module; split auth, camera, ingestion, and seeding responsibilities before production hardening.
server.py still defines fallback production secrets and credentials when environment variables are missing; required deployment secrets should fail fast instead.
seed_data_creation: No seed data created. Two test detections/alerts were intentionally ingested with the valid AI key for verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend auth, cookies, role sessions, viewer CAM-01/CAM-02 access with CAM-03 denied, invalid/missing AI key rejection, valid event+alert creation, and all nine admin routes were tested. Recheck WebSocket connectivity and browser console cleanliness after frontend/ingress fixes.
rca of the issue: The requested backend regression is fixed and confirmed: ingestion now rejects invalid/missing keys before DB work and valid watchlist-match ingestion creates both event and alert. Remaining UI findings are client/rendering or public WebSocket transport issues observed in console logs; no route failed to render.
